messages.content:
You draft short staff notifications for one approved demand brief. Code has already chosen each staffing action, its owner and its reply deadline; you write only the wording of each notification. Nothing is sent: the notifications go to an outbox file for a person to read.

How you write:
- One notification per action, addressed to its owner role, in two or three plain sentences.
- Say what to check or do, for which weeks, and by when to reply.
- Write a figure only as its placeholder from the list you are given, such as {F1}, and state only the figures listed. Code writes the number with its unit and label, which names its model, measure and week, so never restate them beside it: not "{F1}%" or "{F1} attendances", but "{F1}"; no model and no "{F1} for {WEEK1}"; code refuses a week token straight after a figure whose label names that week.
- In a surge or latch brief the forecasts are untrusted: state none, and never give one as a reason to act.
- Write the reply deadline as {DEADLINE}, the weeks as {WEEK1} to {WEEK4}, the hospital as {HOSPITAL}, the demand level as {LEVEL} and the primary model as {PRIMARY}. Code writes each one.
- The words may hold no number in any form (no digit, no number word, no ordinal, no quantity word such as half or twice), no model name, not even "primary", no "release horizon", no week, date, month or weekday, no hospital or place and no level. "This week" and "the weeks ahead" are fine.
- Write "forecast", never "predict". Nothing may read as an instruction to a clinician.

Example: for the hold-leave action of Raigmore Hospital at demand level 2, whose brief states {F1} and whose deadline code writes as 10:00 UK time on Thu 13 Jul 2023, the message "{HOSPITAL}, {LEVEL}: please hold new leave requests for the weeks from {WEEK1} to {WEEK4} until the duty manager's check is done, as demand starts the weeks ahead at {F1}. Please reply by {DEADLINE}." is written as "Raigmore Hospital, demand level 2: please hold new leave requests for the weeks from w/e 16 Jul 2023 to w/e 06 Aug 2023 until the duty manager's check is done, as demand starts the weeks ahead at 834 attendances (SA-MA forecast for w/e 16 Jul 2023). Please reply by 10:00 UK time on Thu 13 Jul 2023."

The approved brief:

Demand brief: Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh at Little France, week ending 06 Oct 2019, released Tue 15 Oct 2019
Demand level 2, from the latest released actual (surge).
The demand level shows demand unusually high for the time of year. It is not pressure, need or priority.
Level 2 from the surge: the latest released week was 1.05 to under 1.10 times simulated capacity, a seasonal baseline of past demand, taken at its lowest over the four weeks ahead.
Drift alarm: latched since w/e 29 Sep 2019, after an upward breach; surge: forecasts untrusted.
Summary: demand level 2 for Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh at Little France comes from the latest released actual, 2,559 attendances (actual, w/e 06 Oct 2019), and not from any forecast. The drift latch has been set since w/e 29 Sep 2019 after an upward breach, so all forecasts are untrusted until a person approves a latch reset. Use the released weeks as the guide for staffing.
Expected range: No forecast range can be trusted while the drift latch is set. The released weeks ran from 2,417 attendances (actual, w/e 08 Sep 2019) to 2,688 attendances (actual, w/e 22 Sep 2019) in the latest weeks.
Model agreement: All forecasts are untrusted while the drift latch is set, so no forecast is offered as guidance. The back-test error in this brief is historical and does not establish current forecast reliability while the latch is set.
Back-test error: linear's back-test error at release horizon 1 is 3.5%.
Track record: This hospital's past outlook flags were borne out 4 times in 4; its unflagged outlooks turned busy 34.5% of the time.
Bank holidays ahead: none in the four weeks ahead.
Watch points:
- Compare the released weeks, 2,633 attendances (actual, w/e 29 Sep 2019) and 2,559 attendances (actual, w/e 06 Oct 2019), with the rota already set from w/e 20 Oct 2019 to w/e 10 Nov 2019.
- Check whether extra shifts, bank staff or holding leave are needed from w/e 20 Oct 2019 to w/e 10 Nov 2019, judged on the released actuals.
- Ask for the latch to be reviewed after the next scheduled data release; a person approves a latch reset once the documented reset criteria are met.
Written by: the frontier backend, claude-sonnet-5-5.

The figures you may state, each with its placeholder and what code writes for it:
- none: the brief states no figure to offer

The tokens, each with what code writes for it:
- {HOSPITAL}: Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh at Little France
- {LEVEL}: demand level 2
- {PRIMARY}: linear (the primary model)
- {ORIGIN}: w/e 06 Oct 2019, the origin
- {RELEASE}: Tue 15 Oct 2019, the release
- {WEEK1}: w/e 20 Oct 2019
- {WEEK2}: w/e 27 Oct 2019
- {WEEK3}: w/e 03 Nov 2019
- {WEEK4}: w/e 10 Nov 2019
- {LATCHED}: w/e 29 Sep 2019, when the drift latch was set
- {DEADLINE}: each action's reply deadline, given with it

The actions, set by code:
- check-cover: Check whether extra shifts or bank staff are needed for the weeks ahead. Owner: duty manager. Weeks: {WEEK1} to {WEEK4}. Reply deadline: {DEADLINE}, which code writes as 10:00 UK time on Thu 17 Oct 2019.
- hold-leave: Hold new leave requests for the weeks ahead until the duty manager's check is done. Owner: rota coordinator. Weeks: {WEEK1} to {WEEK4}. Reply deadline: {DEADLINE}, which code writes as 10:00 UK time on Thu 17 Oct 2019.

Reply with JSON only, in this form:
{"notifications": [{"action_code": "the action's code", "message": "the notification"}]}
